newsitem.title: USA: Northwestern Steel expects difficult Q1.
newsitem.headline: Northwestern Steel expects difficult Q1.

text.p: Northwestern Steel and Wire Co chairman Robert Gurnitz said the company's first quarter of fiscal 1997 will be difficult because of a reduced order intake during the fiscal 1996 fourth quarter.
But Gurnitz said in a statement the company was focused on continuing improvement in its financial performance.

Earlier Thursday Northwestern Steel reported lower July 31 fourth-quarter earnings of $9.9 million or $0.40 per share compared to $17.1 million or $0.67 per share a year ago. The current quarter included $8.8 million or $0.35 per share of tax benefits associated with recognition of deferred tax assets which are not expected to be used.
The prior year's quarter included the benefit of similar tax adjustments amounting to $10.6 million or $0.42 per share.
Gurnitz said, "Fourth quarter earnings before tax adjustments were achieved despite the impact of higher costs and lower margins associated with labor negotiations and a possible work stoppage."
